chapter: Early bands, Calloway to Basie and Kansas City (third typescript)
title: The Subway jam sessions and Piney Brown in Kansas City
summary: Musicians jammed at the Subway at 18th and Pine, run by Piney Brown; Kansas City was a jumping bootleg town during the depression.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: It was a jam. You know -- it was a jam. We used to go to a place down there in Kansas City and jam -- you know. Called The Subway. It was on 18th and Pine. And it's under a place -- under a restaurant named Eleanor's. And she had very good food there. You know -- and it was under there -- a basement
down in there called The Subway. And the guys used to go down there and jam. And the guy that ran it was named Piney Brown (PHONETIC). I don't know if you've ever heard that name.
Yeah. Because Of Pine Brown's Worms. That's what Judd Perry (PHONETIC) made a record out of.
He was -- I guess he was a good friend to a lot of musicians.
Yeah, he was a nice guy.

Ah, it was a jumping town in them days. Those were bootlegging days but they was good days. I don't mean they were -- I didn't make a whole lot of money or anything but -- because the depression was on yet. You know.
It was in the middle of the depression you know. But we -- (inaudible). Well you see -- I met Chuck too down there -- he used to go down there to dance.
